event: At six on a rainy evening, Nala bolts her Weavers' Row shop behind her last customer.

memory.fact: Nala rents a narrow shop on Weavers' Row.

event: Nala turns the window card and sweeps loose threads off the cutting table.
Nala's rent book lies open under the counter at a page she would rather not read again.

memory.fact: Nala is behind on the rent for the shop.

event: Nala lights the lamp over the treadle machine against the rain's dimness.
The bell rings, and the door stands open though its bolt is still shot.
A small woman in a rain-beaded grey cloak steps in and shuts the door with her heel.
She has long dark green hair pinned with birch leaves, pointed ears and eyes greener still.
She carries a bolt of cloth in her arms like a sleeping cat.
In a hill-farm lilt she names Nala the seamstress.
Glancing at the rent book, she says she was told: narrow shop, red hair, behind on the rent.
She unrolls on the cutting table a grey-green silk so fine the lamplight sinks into it.
She asks for a Beltane dance gown made by mortal hands, still a gown at sunrise.

memory.fact: Shaestrel needs a gown for the Beltane dance, made by mortal hands so it is a gown at dawn.
Shaestrel needs a gown for the Beltane dance, made by mortal hands so it is a gown at dawn.
A thing made by mortal hands stays what it is after dawn.

event: She gives Nala three days and says she will not pay in coin.
She offers something better than coin, if Nala will hear it.
Nala tells the woman she is listening to what is better than coin.
The woman's smile opens enough to show the edge of her teeth.
She sits up on the cutting table beside the silk, boots swinging clear of the floor.
The silk slides with her, turning green where it folds and grey again as it settles.

memory.fact: The silk shifts between grey and green as it moves, like new leaves in rain.

event: She tells Nala she is of the Spring Court, as the still-bolted door will have shown.

memory.fact: Shaestrel is a fae of the Spring Court.

event: Her bargain: Nala makes her a gown from this silk with her own hands, done by moonrise on Beltane.
If Nala does it, Nala may ask her for one thing.

memory.fact: Shaestrel's terms: the gown done by moonrise on Beltane night, and Nala may ask her one thing.

event: If it is not done by moonrise, Nala owes the Spring Court a year of sewing across the ford.

memory.fact: If the gown is not done by then, Nala owes the Spring Court a year of sewing across the ford.

event: She wets her thumb and holds it out to Nala, as a bargain is struck at the cattle market.
Nala agrees to the bargain.
The fae laughs and presses her wet thumb to the back of Nala's hand on the table's edge.

memory.fact: Nala and Shaestrel struck the Beltane gown bargain on the evening of April 28.

event: Her skin is cool and smells of cut grass.
For a breath the lamp flame stands tall and still, then flickers on as before.
She slips off the table, unpins her grey cloak and drops it over the stool by the treadle machine.
Under it she wears a pale green dress held up by two green cords, her arms bare.
She says Nala will want her measure, and lifts her arms out from her sides.
Nala says she gives silk only her best work, and asks the fae to strip for exact measurements.
The fae's brows go up, then she grins with all her teeth.
She tells Nala she has not even asked her name.
She tugs loose the cords at each shoulder, and the dress slides down her and is gone.
What lands at her feet is a drift of fresh green birch leaves, like those in her hair.
She steps out of the leaves and lifts her arms again, bare in the lamplight.
Nala takes the tape from her neck and measures from the nape; the fae's skin is cool.
Nala measures shoulders, bust, waist, hips and arm, pencilling each figure into the book.

memory.fact: Nala took Shaestrel's full measure for the gown on April 28, pencilled in her book.

event: The fae hums something low and quick that Nala doesn't know while Nala works.
Nala kneels for the waist-to-floor length, and the leaves crackle under her knee.
The fae looks down over her shoulder and asks if Nala has thought what she'll ask for.
A birch leaf slips from her hair and spins down past Nala's face.
Nala says she won't ask for the fae's name; she must tell it, and Nala thinks she'll enjoy it.
The fae laughs down at Nala, bright and sudden.
She tells Nala her name is Shaestrel, and that Nala may have it for nothing.

memory.fact: She told Nala her name, Shaestrel, on the evening of April 28.

event: Shaestrel crouches among the leaves, face level with Nala's, smelling again of cut grass.
Her eyes go slowly over Nala's face, the way one runs a seam for a dropped stitch.
Shaestrel says Nala will ask her for something with a door in it.
She stands and swings the grey cloak round her shoulders, leaving the leaves where they fell.
She says she'll come back tomorrow when the lamps are lit, for the first fitting.

event: She tells Nala to have something ready for her to stand in.
At the door she slides the bolt back with one finger.
Nala tells Shaestrel, by name, that she'll see her tomorrow.
Shaestrel smiles, quick and pleased, and steps out into the rain.
Nala shoots the bolt home again and turns up the lamp.
She drafts the gown on brown paper from the measures in her book.
She pins the paper pieces to unbleached calico and cuts a toile for the fitting.
At the treadle machine she tacks the toile together with long loose stitches.
She hangs the finished toile on the back-room door, her shoulders aching.

memory.fact: Nala cut and tacked a calico toile of the gown on April 28, ready for the first fitting.
